cottage.name: Cottage
cottage.desc: Wattle, daub and thatch: a hearth, a bed and a pig.

house.name: House
house.desc: A timber-framed house with a tiled roof, and a chimney that draws.

townhouse.name: Townhouse
townhouse.desc: Three stories leaning out over the street. Merchants and masters live here.

shop.name: Shop
shop.desc: A draper, a chandler or a baker, with a sign over the door.

croft.name: Croft
croft.desc: A cottage, a strip of oats and a cow. The family lives on it and sends what it does not eat to the stores.

smallholding.name: Smallholding
smallholding.desc: A longhouse and a byre, a few sheep and a vegetable plot.

grange.name: Grange
grange.desc: A yeoman’s farm with a barn and a dovecote. It feeds a street.

workshop.name: Workshop
workshop.desc: A carpenter’s shop: hafts, rakes, buckets and benches. Wooden tools, and wares for the market.

joinery.name: Joinery
joinery.desc: A cooper and a wheelwright under one roof, with a sawpit in the yard.

guildhall.name: Craft Hall
guildhall.desc: A master’s hall with apprentices: iron-shod tools, locks and hinges, and a counter on the street.

farmstead.name: Farmstead
farmstead.desc: A farmhouse, a barn and a yard. Its hands tend every field within eight tiles, one for each eight tiles of field.

fishery.name: Fisherman’s Hut
fishery.desc: Nets, a jetty and a smoking rack. It must stand by the water.

hunter.name: Hunter’s Lodge
hunter.desc: Venison and hide from the surrounding woods. It wants a forest within ten tiles.

granary.name: Granary
granary.desc: Raised on staddle stones against the rats. Holds a harvest.

mill.name: Windmill
mill.desc: Grinds grain and bakes it into bread: four loaves and a half for every three measures of grain.

brewery.name: Brewery
brewery.desc: Ale for the taverns, and for anyone who can pay.

woodcutter.name: Woodcutter’s Lodge
woodcutter.desc: Fells the trees within nine tiles. The forest grows back, but slowly.

forester.name: Forester’s Lodge
forester.desc: Plants and tends young woods within eight tiles of the lodge, so the woodcutters never run dry. It plants on open ground only: not on streets, zones or in a block.

quarry.name: Quarry
quarry.desc: Cuts stone from the nearby outcrops. It must stand near bare rock.

ironmine.name: Iron Mine
ironmine.desc: A shaft, a windlass and a sledge. It must stand near iron ore.

storehouse.name: Storehouse
storehouse.desc: Timber, stone, iron and everything else that keeps.

smithy.name: Smithy
smithy.desc: Turns iron and charcoal into the tools every trade wears out.

weaver.name: Weaver
weaver.desc: Cloth from the shepherds’ wool. Warm backs make happy ones.

well.name: Well
well.desc: Clean water, and a bucket in reach when something catches fire.

green.name: Village Green
green.desc: A pond, a maypole and a bench. Somewhere to be that is not home.

tavern.name: Tavern
tavern.desc: Ale, a fire and a song. It drinks about a third of a barrel a week for each household near it.

chapel.name: Chapel
chapel.desc: A nave, a bell and a priest. People bear a great deal when they have somewhere to put it.

healer.name: Healer’s Cottage
healer.desc: Herbs, poultices and sound advice. Plague runs slower where she lives.

market.name: Market Square
market.desc: A paved square with a cross at the middle. Merchants will come to trade at your gates once it stands.

watchtower.name: Watchtower
watchtower.desc: A lookout and a brazier. It sees raiders coming and makes the streets feel safe.

barracks.name: Barracks
barracks.desc: Six men-at-arms with the pay and the tools to match. They fight well and eat steadily.

gatehouse.name: Gatehouse
gatehouse.desc: Towers either side of the bridge, a portcullis and a windlass to raise the drawbridge. Build it on an open gate.

cathedral.name: Cathedral
cathedral.desc: Spires you can see from the next county. Faith for a whole barony, and a good deal of standing.

res.name: Housing
res.desc: Cottages and houses grow along the streets, as deep as the plots go. What the houses leave behind them is kitchen garden.

market.name: Market
market.desc: Stalls and shops, which pay the lord in coin and give people something to spend it on.

wheat.name: Wheat
wheat.desc: Open fields of grain, sown in spring and reaped in autumn. They need a farmstead within eight tiles.

veg.name: Gardens
veg.desc: Cabbages, leeks and beans. Quick to grow, quick to spoil. They need a farmstead within eight tiles.

orchard.name: Orchard
orchard.desc: Apple and pear trees that give fruit every autumn and shade all year. They need a farmstead within eight tiles.

pasture.name: Pasture
pasture.desc: Sheep and cattle: wool, and meat in the autumn cull. They need a farmstead within eight tiles.

croft.name: Smallholdings
croft.desc: Crofts along the lane: a family on each, with a strip, a cow and a pig. They feed themselves and send the rest to the stores, with no farmstead needed. They grow when there are hands wanting work.

craft.name: Workshops
craft.desc: Carpenters, coopers and wheelwrights: timber in, tools and wares out, and the wares sold in the town. Workshops grow when there are hands wanting work. Keep them back from the houses: they catch fire.

CASTLE_LEVELS.name: Timber Keep
CASTLE_LEVELS.desc: A palisade on a mound and a keep of oak. Enough to hold a hamlet.

CASTLE_LEVELS.name: Stone Keep
CASTLE_LEVELS.desc: A keep of dressed stone, a curtain wall and a tower at each corner.

CASTLE_LEVELS.name: Castle
CASTLE_LEVELS.desc: A great hall, an inner ward and walls two men wide.

CASTLE_LEVELS.name: Citadel
CASTLE_LEVELS.desc: Concentric walls, a barbican and a hall fit for a king’s cousin.

dirt.name: Dirt Road
dirt.desc: Beaten earth. Cheap, and it turns to mud in the rain.

bridge.name: Bridge
bridge.desc: A plank bridge over a river or a lake: drag from one bank to the other, up to six tiles of water, in a straight line. Both ends must be on dry land. The moat is crossed only at the gates.

cobble.name: Cobbled Road
cobble.desc: Paving stones laid in sand. Dry in any weather, and a good address.
